analysis_type: Pre-specified lead-lag sensitivity analysis using the baseline meeting-fixed-effects VAR-style regressions
forbidden_actions: Selecting, adding, dropping, reordering, or changing specifications based on statistical significance.
Selecting offsets, equations, samples, controls, or reporting subsets based on p values, t statistics, coefficient magnitude, or any favorable result.
Modifying, replacing, deleting, or creating files or source data under validation/.
Modifying the canonical validated panel or silently substituting another input dataset.
Pairing observations across FOMC meeting boundaries.
Changing the baseline estimator, own-market controls, meeting fixed effects, HAC bandwidth, or offset set.
Adding unregistered offsets, placebo tests, trimming rules, transformations, or alternative specifications.
Omitting failed, insufficient, null, reversed, adverse, or non-estimable offset results.
Overwriting evidence from experiments 002 through 007 or any existing experiment-008 artifacts.

interpretation_rules: Interpret the profile descriptively and do not select an offset, equation, or subset based on p values or any other favorable result.

A profile concentrated at contemporaneous or past FF revisions for the IEM equation, together with weak or absent future-predictor and reverse-direction profiles, is consistent with the preregistered timing hypothesis.

A flat, symmetric, reverse-direction, or future-predictor-dominated profile is adverse evidence against a temporal price-discovery interpretation and supports treating the baseline association as fragile or nonspecific.
A contemporaneous profile alone cannot distinguish rapid causal transmission from simultaneous responses to common information.
Offset-specific sample differences must be reported and must not be interpreted as a clean causal comparison.
Null, reversed, adverse, and non-estimable results remain valid outcomes and must not be discarded.
Even if the preregistered profile is supported, the result does not establish independent confirmation or causal price discovery because the analysis covers only eight meetings.
The existing interpretation of the historical exercise as a robustness stress test is unchanged unless materially stronger evidence is established outside this experiment.
P values and statistical significance are not model-selection criteria and do not determine which results are reported or emphasized.
pairing_rules: Use the canonical validated historical panel at the frozen path under validation/external/barchart/processed/historical_panel_2002_gap_safe.csv.
Reproduce the baseline before constructing or estimating any offset-specific model.
For each outcome at observation t, retain the baseline own-market lag at t-1 unchanged.
Replace only the baseline cross-market revision regressor with the cross-market revision at t-k.
Interpret k=0 as contemporaneous, k>0 as a predictor preceding the outcome, and k<0 as a predictor following the outcome.
Use a shifted predictor only when its source observation exists within the same family or FOMC meeting as the outcome.
Require the baseline lag observation and the shifted cross-market predictor to be revision-valid.
Do not pair observations across meeting boundaries, excluded temporal gaps, or unrelated family blocks.
Preserve the baseline meeting fixed-effect construction and omit no meeting or offset after inspecting results.
Estimate both directional equations for every pre-specified offset, even when a coefficient is null, reversed, unstable, insufficiently supported, or non-estimable.
Use HAC covariance with bandwidth 6 and the same within-meeting block handling as the frozen baseline.
Treat offset-specific samples as distinct samples and report their exact row counts and included-meeting counts.
